segments.source: Cold brew is a brewing method, not a roast category. A coarse grind steeps in cool water for hours before filtering; the bean still determines the roaster’s flavor target. We looked for exact US whole-bean identity, a current official cold-brew recommendation or collection placement, a distinct buyer job, a linked full review and a material reason to skip. Blue Bottle Three Africas and Giant Steps meet those criteria as two different first-bag decisions.

segments.source: Use a coarse grind, weighed coffee and water, a clean food-safe vessel and a complete filtration step. Stumptown’s cold-brew guidance describes 12–24 hours as a broad route; Peet’s product panels use 12-plus hours. Neither is a promise that one fixed time suits every bean, vessel, grind and refrigerator. Record the water temperature, time and concentrate dilution before judging a second bag.
segments.context: Use a coarse grind, weighed coffee and water, a clean food-safe vessel and a complete filtration step. Stumptown’s cold-brew guidance describes 12–24 hours as a broad route; Peet’s product panels use 12-plus hours. Neither is a promise that one fixed time suits every bean, vessel, grind and refrigerator. Record the water temperature, time and concentrate dilution before judging a second bag. [8] [4]

segments.source: A cold-steep concentrate and a ready-to-drink cold brew are different ratios. If you add ice or milk, write down that serving dilution too. A stronger steep can taste weak after heavy dilution, while a fine grind or poor filtration can make any bean seem muddy. Change one variable at a time; do not copy Giant Steps’ French-press-with-milk 1:13 figure into a cold-brew recipe.

segments.source: Filter and refrigerate the finished drink promptly according to the brewing equipment’s food-safety guidance. The long steep is not an excuse to leave an opened bag in heat or sunlight. Grind only what the batch needs and check the actual roast date when the whole beans arrive.

segments.source: Three Africas is the fruit-led path. Blue Bottle names golden raisin, winey blueberry and lemon zest and says its washed and natural Ethiopian components and Central African coffee make a cold-brewed blend with depth. These are attributed descriptions, not tasting notes from Coffeedant. If you drink black cold brew, its intended fruit direction is easier to test without milk.
segments.context: Three Africas is the fruit-led path. Blue Bottle names golden raisin, winey blueberry and lemon zest and says its washed and natural Ethiopian components and Central African coffee make a cold-brewed blend with depth. These are attributed descriptions, not tasting notes from Coffeedant. If you drink black cold brew, its intended fruit direction is easier to test without milk. [1]

segments.source: Giant Steps is the dark, milk-oriented path. Blue Bottle lists cocoa, toasted marshmallow and graham cracker and places it in the cold-brew collection. The roaster also gives a separate French-press-with-milk suggestion. We infer it is a more natural starting point for a milk-diluted dark cup; that inference is not a measured claim that it beats Three Africas in any recipe.

segments.source: A 12 oz bag is about 340 g. At 30 g per batch it provides roughly eleven theoretical batches before grinder loss; concentrate recipes can consume more. Those are arithmetic illustrations, not Coffeedant recipes or serving-size promises. Start with one bag and calculate from your actual dose, dilution and drinking frequency.
